dedupe_keys.name: winter flow synthetic hospital surge model

description: WINTER-Flow is a Python and Streamlit application published by the jiff3 maintainer for exploring respiratory-wave pressure on a synthetic hospital network. Seeded generators create fictional hospitals, staffing, transfers and patient arrivals, while SimPy models patient flow with one simulation unit equal to an hour. Users choose virus and intervention scenarios and inspect emergency-department waits, ward/ICU occupancy and staff-pressure indicators. Forecasting and an approximate candidate-search optimiser support scenario comparison, with CSV and Markdown reporting. Coverage is a user-defined fictional network with no real observation period or calibrated hospital geography. Public source and installation instructions are free under MIT. The README explicitly limits the application to synthetic exploration and says it must not support actual hospital operations or patient-care decisions. Its forecasts, risk scores and intervention ranking are simplified and unvalidated for that purpose. The resource supports research into capacity and resource-allocation assumptions, complementing the catalogue's SimPy healthcare examples (model-simpy-streamlit-healthcare-des). A digital-twin label does not establish connection to a physical hospital. No model execution or clinical data access occurred.
